note: Attacker-controlled bytes are wrapped in a QBuffer and reused as the backing store for all archive handlers.
The same buffer is also exposed through a gzip decompression device, so gzip parsing is driven directly by the attacker input.
Each archive handler is opened on the shared buffer, causing KArchive to inspect the input as a compressed archive.
GZip mode configures zlib to auto-detect and consume gzip headers before inflating the payload.
The attacker-controlled compressed stream is handed to zlib inflate, which reaches the vulnerable fast-path during decompression.
